title: I built a top-down tactical shooter with its own engine, coding it with AI agents. The free demo is out
author: catinrage
selftext:
Scrim is a top-down tactical shooter where every light casts a shadow: you see only what your soldier sees, footsteps give you away, and cover has a height that bullets, sight and blasts all respect. You can build walls and sentry turrets, drive a Humvee, fly a drone and fight through rain at night.

Link to demo : [https://catinrage.itch.io/scrim](https://catinrage.itch.io/scrim)

How it's made:

* **No engine.** TypeScript on Bun, with a WebGL2 renderer and WebAudio written by hand. The desktop app is Electron.
* **Code:** written with Claude Code agents. I plan the work and review it; agents each work on their own branch, and a merge gate only lands a branch when the type check and the test suite pass. The project is now about 470,000 lines of TypeScript with around 900 test files.
* **Keeping AI code sane:** the simulation is deterministic and runs server-side even in single player, with a golden-master replay test, so a change that breaks gameplay shows up in the tests, not in a player's match.
* **Sound:** announcer voices, many sound effects and the trailer's music were made with ElevenLabs.
* **Time:** 2 months



The demo has seven modes against bots (tutorial, sandbox, team deathmatch, a bomb-defusal mode, a heist, zombie waves and a random-rules mode). It's free on [itch.io](http://itch.io) for Windows and Linux; the link is in the first comment.

Happy to answer anything about the workflow, what worked and what the agents got wrong.
